rationale: Round-2 regression check of ada49e53 under the codebase-pin lens, as the round-1 zero-ask approver. All round-1 asks touching my lens are ADDRESSED with real, hermetic, red-on-revert tests. (1) Test inventory: 15 new tests land in the fix commit (4 draft_test.go: G2a recovered-epic, G2a genuine-no-epic compat, G5 multi-draft sorted, G3 branch-only-draft; 6 state_show_honesty_test.go: 3 G1 flag-blind legs, G1 flagged-nonexistent refusal, G2b transient-flake retry, G5 state-layer ambiguity; 4 gitutil fileexists_test.go; 1 instruct run_mode_error_test.go) — all pass uncached, and the full `go test -count=1 -short ./...` suite is green from the bead worktree, which was left byte-identical (git status clean). (2) Hermetic: every fixture root is t.TempDir(); bd via the phase seams with t.Cleanup restore; git via pinned -c identity + LookPath-skip; gitutil tests use the existing swapExec/initGitRepo/swapRealExecCommand house harness; setStateShowSpecFlag/resetStateShowFlags guard cobra state. No PATH games anywhere. (3) Red-on-revert PROBED on four hunks, including both mandated targets: a /tmp archive with the two G1 state.go hunks and the G4 run.go check reverted fails TestStateShow_FlaggedNonexistentSpec_RefusesInsteadOfIdle (the mandated G1 probe), TestStateShow_FlagBlind_UnresolvableSpecWithOneDraft_Refuses, and TestRun_ModeResolutionFailure_FallsBackGracefully (the mandated G4 probe); a second archive with the PRE-FIX 7b6d83f1 resolve.go swapped in fails TestResolveModeWithCache_TransientFirstCallFailure_FindsRecoveredEpic (G2a) and TestDraftSpecStatusWithCache_BranchOnlyDraft_VisibleViaTreeProbe (G3) while the compatibility leg (GenuineNoEpicStillProbesDraft) correctly stays green both ways. (4) newBranchOnlyDraftFixture genuinely reproduces spec create's shape: verified against internal/spec/create.go:104-143 — InitSpecWorkspace (branch + separate worktree), spec dir + spec.md written and CommitAll'd ONLY in the workspace, never the invoking checkout; the fixture's worktree-add/-write/-commit/-remove is that mechanism minus CLI wrapping, and its premise assertion (os.Stat of the root's own SpecDir must miss) pins it. (5) The cat-file -e exit-code claim FileExistsAtRef's branch-confirmed-first ordering depends on was re-verified empirically in a scratch repo: absent-path AND absent-ref both exit 128, present exits 0 — the ordering in draftSpecStatusWithCache (BranchExistsIn before any tree probe) is load-bearing and correctly implemented. (6) The two new ratchet allowlist entries (FileExistsAtRef exec site; specTreeCandidatePaths .mindspec/specs/ literal) are house-pattern-conformant and their justification claims are true in code: both operands RejectOptionLike-gated pre-composition, and specID reaches specTreeCandidatePaths only after workspace.SpecBranch's idvalidate gate earlier in the same function. Round-1 ask classification for my slot: R2-F1 ADDRESSED (G1 refusal, tested + probed red), R2-F2 ADDRESSED (G4 run.go fallback, tested + probed red), R2-F3 ADDRESSED (G5 at both layers), R2-F4's no-fabrication conclusion still holds under the reordered probe. No MISSED, no NEW_ISSUE blocking.

findings.title: Two G1 flag-blind tests refuse via an incidental error path on their non-git fixture roots
findings.detail: TestStateShow_FlagBlind_UnresolvableSpecWithNoDrafts_Refuses and TestStateShow_FlagBlind_InvalidSpecValue_Refuses use a bare t.TempDir + .mindspec dir (no git repo). Against the true pre-fix baseline (7b6d83f1, where draft discovery never called git) they would be red as intended, but under a SURGICAL removal of only the specFlag-propagation guard they stay green: the fallback's DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache now calls gitutil.LocalBranchRefs, which errors on a non-git root, producing a refusal for the wrong reason (verified in my probe: both passed with the G1 hunks reverted while the two git-repo-rooted G1 tests went red). The load-bearing G1 legs (one-draft flag-blind, flagged-nonexistent) are robustly red-on-revert, so this is hardening only: give these two fixtures a baseline git repo (newBareGitRepo already exists in the same file) so their refusal can only come from the guard under test.

findings.title: The G1 guard comment's 'worktree-derived spec ID always probes to at least spec mode' is not strictly true for a damaged state
findings.detail: The refusal guard fires only when specFlag != "". A spec worktree whose spec/<id> branch was deleted while the worktree (and its spec dir) lingers resolves the specID from worktree identity (no flag), then fails the draft probe at the branch check (branch is required first) and derives idle — rendering idle+activeSpec with no refusal, contrary to the comment's universal claim. Operator-damaged edge state, pre-existing class, and arguably R6/bead-4-table territory rather than this fix's; flagging so the comment's claim is not read as a proven invariant.

findings.title: spec create's warn-only CommitAll leaves a commit-less draft invisible from main — consistent with G3's contract, noting for the record
findings.detail: internal/spec/create.go:141-143 only WARNS if the auto-commit fails, leaving spec/<id> pointing at the baseline commit with the spec.md unstaged in the (still-present) spec worktree. From main such a draft is branch-exists + tree-probe-miss + dir-miss = not a draft, i.e. invisible to the new discovery. That matches G3's deliberate contract (branch + COMMITTED content) and the operator is standing in the worktree where AC-1(i) discovery works, so no change requested — recorded so the boundary is a known decision, not an oversight.
